text:
marta: Heads up — hitting a cluster of Xid 48 + 79 on eu-central embedder pool since 09:12 UTC. Seen on 3 different hosts in rack euc-12, all on A10p. Pattern looks tied to a bursty tenant doing large batched embeddings.
lee: saw the alert, thanks. Any kernel/dmesg snippets?
omar: paste from one host: 
```
# dmesg | tail -n 10
[12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00:00): 48, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[12345.678921] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00:00): 79, GPU exception on channel 0x1a
[12345.679002] pci 0000:3b:00.0: enabling device (0000 -> 0003)
[12345.679103] kernel: pcieport 0000:00:1c.7: AER: Corrected error received: id=0008
```
ryan: interesting — we also saw NIC interrupts / link flaps at the same time in the switch logs. Possible power/PCIe stress.
jess: tenant id 0x7f3 pushed a huge embedding batch at 09:11 via /v1/embeddings, size ~120k tokens across 3 requests.
marta: correlating tenant + optype: heavy contiguous allocation then immediate reclaim, repeated. Hypothesis: memory fragmentation + driver bug under high SBM (single-batch multi-seq) loads causes GPU reset (Xid 48) then exception (79). Switch logs suggest a simultaneous PCIe AER event.
omar: quick triage results: only A10p machines affected, not H100 fleet. No ECC counters beyond corrected errors. Card temps normal.
lee: can we repro? create a controlled job that mimics tenant batch sizes and see if it triggers on staging rig.
ryan: I spun up a staging A10p and replayed the tenant load (same batch shapes) — reproduced Xid 48 within 90s. Also saw a single AER corrected error preceding the Xid.
sre-bot: alert: rack euc-12 has 3 hosts in degraded state; routing set to reduce embedder traffic by 30% to eu-west fallback.
jess: routing is live. We should avoid broad drains without perf headroom — customers will see latency.
marta: proposed mitigations (short term):
- throttle per-tenant batch size (limit to 8k tokens per request) and enforce rate limits for embeddings.
- auto-route heavy embedder tenants to dedicated A10 pool with higher headroom.
- schedule graceful drain + pci rescan on the 3 hosts overnight if they stay flaky.
omar: driver/firmware notes — current driver 535.86 and fw 55.1101 on A10p. There's a newer FW 55.1302 with fixes for PCIe AER under heavy contiguous allocation. Worth a canary.
lee: agree on canary. Suggest rollout plan: escalate 1 host to firmware 55.1302 in eu-west staging, run replay for 24h, then target rack if stable.
ryan: if firmware doesn't help, plan B is card swap or escalate to vendor RMA. But swapping has capacity and cost implications — we should try software mitigations first.
jess: ops question — how much spare capacity if we drain 3 hosts in eu-central? We may need to burst to other regions which ups inter-region egress costs.
infra-bot: current spare capacity (A10p) in eu-central: 2 nodes; fallback to eu-west available with +18ms median and +$0.023/token estimate for embeddings if routed cross-region.
marta: cost tradeoff note: routing to eu-west increases per-tenant cost but reduces error exposure. Recommend temporary automatic routing for the offending tenant until a fix.
omar: action items:
- @ryan: run firmware canary on eu-west staging (owner) — target start 2024-05-02 02:00 UTC.
- @lee: add per-tenant batch limiter and alert on any tenant > 8k tokens (owner).
- @jess: coordinate with customer success to throttle tenant 0x7f3 and notify tenant (owner).
- @marta: schedule graceful drain of the 3 eu-central hosts if instability persists after canary (owner).
- @omar: collect full nvml, dmesg, switch AER logs and upload to /infra/troubleshooting/euc-12/xid-48-79/ (owner).
ryan: I'll also run a synthetic with varying batch shapes to map which shapes trigger earlier failures.
lee: short-term mitigation deployed: per-request batch cap enforced at edge via tokenizer step + 429 with Retry-After.
jess: thanks — I've opened a support ticket with vendor referencing FW 55.1302 and our repro. Ticket #NV-87612.
sre-bot: update: routing policy applied for tenant 0x7f3 -> eu-west until 2024-05-03T12:00Z.
marta: if canary is green, we'll plan a rolling firmware upgrade for the rack during a maintenance window. If not, prepare spare card procurement and RMA path.
omar: final observation — Xid 48 often shows as "GPU has fallen off the bus" which maps to PCIe link or power glitch. Given NIC AER entries, likely board peripheral/integration-level stress. Firmware may help but plan for replace if noise persists.
lee: noted. I'll post an updated short runbook after the canary with exact commands we used for repro + logs to collect.
ryan: thanks all, I'll start the synthetic matrix now.
marta: thanks team — keep updates in this thread. :thumbsup:
